items: Distinguish between 'Charged upon' (non-votable) and 'Made from' the Consolidated Fund of India for exam questions.
Special Majority for removal requires majority of total membership of the House AND at least two-thirds of members present and voting.
While the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge, other Election Commissioners can be removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC.
The Governor does NOT enjoy security of tenure and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional authorities like the CAG, CEC, and UPSC Chairman hold office for a maximum term of six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Salaries and administrative expenses of key constitutional bodies are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to parliamentary vote.
Security of tenure is guaranteed to ensure independence; removal requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Service conditions and salaries of constitutional office holders cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment, except during a Financial Emergency under Article 360.
Post-retirement restrictions apply to posts like the CAG and UPSC Chairman, making them ineligible for further appointment under the Union or State Governments.
